status: proposed repository/content-container architecture for owner approval
goal: Reduce agent confusion and learner-facing sprawl without deleting research, lineage, historical bodies, or specialist knowledge.

review_layer.purpose: Course-2/3 and domain-depth material classified as modules, references, or future advanced candidates; not normal beginner catalog.
Common leadership foundation plus department-specific review packs; no automatic appointment or craft authority.
Stage management, production management, venue operations, paperwork, communication, scheduling, budget/change-control, and post-show learning material under owner/practitioner review.
Rigging, production power/electrical, automation, effects, network/cyber, and other bounded specialist-awareness material.

research_layer.purpose: decision substrates, catalogs, classifications, readiness and gap analysis
cross-system authority/provenance contracts and relationship maps
branch/course/history discovery without converting history into publication authority
proposed pipeline/container/orchestration contracts; PR-first until accepted

archive_policy.preferred_cleanup: index and classify first; optionally prune truly redundant refs only after an accepted stable release and explicit owner approval

naming_rules: Use learner-facing names for public containers and internal state names only in research/review surfaces.
Do not encode Course 2/Course 3 as a required universal product ladder.
Keep historical IDs stable; aliases resolve lineage instead of destructive renames.
Generated files and canonical source data must be visibly distinguishable by path/manifest metadata.
Every off-main archive consulted by agents must have an explicit branch-state classification or retrieval reason.
execution_note: This document intentionally does not move/delete files yet. Physical repository restructuring is a below-visible-surface change and should occur only after owner approval of the container model, with migration validation and lineage preservation.
